description: This episode examines the 1858 joint paper by Charles Darwin and Alfred Russell Wallace that first publicly announced the theory of natural selection, exploring how both men independently arrived at the same revolutionary mechanism for evolution. It covers the core logic of natural selection (variation, heredity, overproduction, and deep time), addresses common misconceptions, and reveals the critical gap in their theory—the mechanism of heredity—that wasn't resolved until Mendel's work on genes and later the discovery of DNA structure. Essential listening for anyone interested in evolutionary biology, the history of scientific discovery, or how transformative ideas develop and mature over time.
